resources.string: Capillary tuft
Glomerular tuft and its blood vessels
Afferent arteriole
Blood enters at the vascular pole through this arteriole, which branches into the capillary tuft.
Efferent arteriole
Capillary branches reunite and blood leaves through this arteriole at the same pole.
Capillary loops
The tuft is a branching network of capillaries. Their porous endothelial lining, basement membrane, and the podocyte foot processes together form the filtration barrier.
Capsule layers
Bowman\'s capsule and its urinary pole
Parietal layer
A single layer of flat cells forms the outer wall. At the urinary pole it becomes continuous with the lining of the proximal tubule.
Visceral layer
Podocytes form the inner layer. Their branching processes wrap individual glomerular capillaries rather than lining the outer wall.
Capsular space
Filtrate collects in the gap between the two layers and enters the proximal tubule at the urinary pole, opposite the vascular pole.
Brush border
Proximal tubule: cortical coils and open wall
Cortical coil
The proximal convoluted tubule begins at the urinary pole. It winds through the cortex and continues as a straighter segment before narrowing into the thin descending limb.
Cuboidal lining
A single layer of cuboidal cells surrounds the lumen. Their apical surfaces face inward, and their bases rest on a basement membrane.
Brush border
Dense microvilli project from the apical surface into the lumen. They give the lining a brush-like edge and increase its surface area.
Loop limbs
Long nephron loop from cortex to medulla and back
Thin descending limb
Below the proximal straight segment, the tubule narrows. A single layer of flat cells lines this limb as it runs deeper into the medulla.
Thin ascending limb
At the hairpin turn of this long loop, the thin-walled tubule reverses direction. The thin ascending limb runs back toward the cortex before its wall thickens.
Thick ascending limb
The ascending wall becomes a single layer of cuboidal cells. The thick limb continues into the cortex and then becomes the distal convoluted tubule.
